Enum Class ScreenKind

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<ScreenKind>
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ScreenKind
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<ScreenKind>, Constable
public enum ScreenKind extends Enum<ScreenKind>
The kind of screen an element is on, which decides how it draws (6.1.0). There is one set of elements; each draws itself for the kind of screen it is on. No element, panel or screen picks a look any other way.
  • CONTAINER: inventories, chests, anything built on vanilla's AbstractContainerScreen. MenuKit's own look: raised grey controls on a light grey panel, dark text without a shadow.
  • OPTIONS: the screens reached from the pause menu and the title screen (Options, Video Settings, Controls, Create World). Vanilla's look there: its stone buttons, checkbox, tab and slot sprites, white text with a shadow, its separators and darker list background, over the blurred world or the panorama.

Where the kind comes from (of(Screen))

  • A panel injected into a vanilla screen: the host knows. An AbstractContainerScreen is a container screen, any other vanilla screen an options screen, so a panel on Controls gets the options look with no code.
  • A slot group's panels: container.
  • A standalone MKScreen: the kind it declared when it was created (super(title, ScreenKind.OPTIONS, panels)), CONTAINER when it declared none, which is how every standalone screen looked before 6.1.0.
  • The HUD: CONTAINER, the look it has always had.
  • A dialog or overlay follows the screen it opens on, since it is a panel on that screen; so does the item chooser an ItemPicker opens.

What the kind changes

Drawing only, never size or behaviour: a panel's background, every control's sprite and every text colour. A piece with no vanilla twin (a radio button, a colour swatch, an info box, a consumer's own sprite) keeps MenuKit's drawing on both kinds; only its text follows the kind.

    • of

      public static ScreenKind of(@Nullable net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      The kind of screen. Every host on a screen, and every screen MenuKit opens over another, uses this. A standalone MKScreen is the kind it declared; any other container screen is CONTAINER; any other screen is OPTIONS. No screen (the HUD, the game itself) is CONTAINER.

    • textColor

      public int textColor(TextRole role)
      The colour of text in role on this kind's surface. Container: dark grey (ElementConstants.TEXT_DARK) for headings and body, ElementConstants.TEXT_MUTED, ElementConstants.TEXT_DISABLED. Options: vanilla's own CommonColors, white for headings and body (the Options title, a setting's name), GRAY for secondary lines (the world list's details) and LIGHT_GRAY for disabled text (an inactive button's label).

    • textShadow

      public boolean textShadow()
      Whether text on this kind's surface has a drop shadow: an options screen's does (vanilla's menu text), a container's does not (vanilla's container labels).
